03/07/2020

Dr Jane Bradshaw

Child Psychiatrist

Wickham Tce

Spring Hill

Brisbane

Dear Dr Bradshaw,

Re: Jackson Martin, DOB: 12/03/2011

I am writing to request full psychiatric assessment for Jackson, who is manifesting a clinical picture
suggestive of autistic spectrum disorder.

Regarding Jackson’s family and social backgrounds, Hhis parents divorced in 2016 for which and he lives
with his mother and step-father with two step brothers. His mother has a history of drug abuse, binge
drinking and depression. He attends year three in primary school, and he has difficulty in making friends,
interacting and picking up on social cues. He is disruptive during class, and he has repetitive behaviour.
Please note, he has had a developmental delay in speech and language assessment at the age of three.

On 20/01/2015, Jackson was brought in by his parents concerning concerned about his speech as he
only can say individual words and short sentences without full sentences. Speech and language
assessment revealed delayed speech, for which a referral to a speech therapist was arranged. Six
months later, he had no improvement, and but his hearing assessment was normal. He has been out of
town since then as his family moved for work.

20/8/20 9:05 AM

Comment [1]: This is an uncountable noun
in this context so it is not used in plural form.

20/8/20 8:51 AM

Comment [2]: This relative clause structure
does not work here. You could use “because
of which, he lives”, but it is more natural to
just use ‘and’ here.

20/8/20 8:54 AM
Comment [3]: This is not really necessary
as you already mentioned short sentences
just before.

20/8/20 8:56 AM

Today, Jackson had an argument and fight fought with other childrens, and he had been progressing
poorly in school over the past two terms for about which his teachers were concerned. His parents were
disturbed due to his angry behaviour, and he spends prolonged time alone playing with one toy only. On
examination, he had a vague facial expression, no eye contact and a minimal response to questions.

Comment [4]: Children is already plural so
you do not need to add ‘s’.

20/8/20 8:56 AM
